questions.question: [NEET 2020 | Biology] The logistic growth model is represented by the equation:
questions.solution: # Answer: **(B) dN/dt = rN(K\u₂₂₁₂N)/K** --- ## Step-by-Step Explanation ### What is Logistic Growth? Logistic growth occurs when a population grows **exponentially at first**, but then **slows down** as it approaches the **carrying capacity (K)** of the environment. ### Breaking Down Option (B): dN/dt = rN(K\u₂₂₁₂N)/K | Component | Meaning | |-----------|---------| | **dN/dt** | Rate of population change | | **r** | Intrinsic rate of increase | | **N** | Population size at time t | | **K** | Carrying capacity (maximum population) | | **(K\u₂₂₁₂N)/K** | Environmental resistance factor | ### Why This Equation Makes Sense: **When N is small** (far from K): - (K\u₂₂₁₂N)/K \u₂₂₄₈₁ - dN/dt \u₂₂₄₈ rN (exponential growth) **When N approaches K** (near carrying capacity): - (K\u₂₂₁₂N)/K \u₂₂₄₈₀ - dN/dt \u₂₂₄₈₀ (growth slows down) **When N = K** (at carrying capacity): - dN/dt = 0 (no growth) --- ## Why Other Options are Wrong: | Option | Why Wrong | |--------|-----------| | **(A)** | This is **exponential growth** (no carrying capacity limit). Ignores environmental resistance. | | **(C)** | This is the **solution to exponential growth**, not logistic growth | | **(D)** | This is one possible **integrated solution** to the logistic equation under specific initial conditions (N\u₂₀₈₀ << K), but not the standard differential equation | --- ## Key Formula to Remember: **Logistic Growth Differential Equation:** \boxed\fracdNdt = rN\frac(K-N)K This is the **Verhulst model** taught in NCERT Class 12 Biology (Chapter: Organisms and Populations).

questions.question: [NEET 2016 | Biology] Correct statement:

options.C: Olonisation of bare rock is primary succession

questions.solution: # Answer: **(B) Lichen is mutualism** --- ## Why This Is Correct \u₂₇₁₃ **Lichens** are composite organisms formed by a **symbiotic association between**: - **Algae or Cyanobacteria** (photosynthetic partner) - **Fungus** (structural partner) **Benefits to both partners:** | Partner | Benefit | |---------|---------| | **Algae/Cyanobacteria** | Protected from harsh conditions; access to water and minerals | | **Fungus** | Food (carbohydrates) from photosynthesis | This is a **book example of MUTUALISM** where both organisms benefit equally. --- ## Why Others Are Wrong \u₂₇₁₇ | Option | Issue | |--------|-------| | **(A) Mycorrhizae = commensalism** | Mycorrhizae are **mutualism**, not commensalism. Both fungi and plant roots benefit mutually. | | **(C) Bare rock colonisation** | While this IS primary succession, the statement is incomplete/vague compared to option B's clarity. | | **(D) Predation = symbiosis** | **False relationship.** Predation is antagonistic (+/\u₂₂₁₂), not symbiosis. Symbiosis requires organisms living together beneficially. | --- ## Key Formula to Remember **Types of Symbiosis:** - **Mutualism:** (+/+) Both benefit \u₂₁₉₂ Lichen, Mycorrhizae, Nitrogen-fixing bacteria in legumes - **Commensalism:** (+/0) One benefits, other unaffected \u₂₁₉₂ Remoras on sharks - **Parasitism:** (+/\u₂₂₁₂) One benefits, other harmed \u₂₁₉₂ Tapeworms, mosquitoes - **Predation:** (+/\u₂₂₁₂) Not symbiosis; one kills the other
